title: Word Search II
description:
Given an m x n board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words on the board.

Each word must be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once in a single word.

The returned words may be given in any order.

examples.explanation: "oath" and "eat" can each be traced through orthogonally adjacent cells without reusing a cell, while "pea" and "rain" cannot.
"abcb" cannot be formed without reusing a cell.

constraints: board[i][j] is a lowercase English letter.
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All the strings of words are unique.
approach: Insert every dictionary word into a trie so a single board path can represent a shared prefix of many words at once, and exploration stops immediately when no word continues the current prefix. Run DFS from each cell, descending the matching trie branch; temporarily mark a visited cell with '#' so it is not reused within one word, then restore it on backtrack. When a trie node holds a terminal word, record it and remove the terminal marker to avoid duplicate answers; pruning empty branches speeds later searches. With S the total dictionary character count, R*C the board size, and L the longest word, worst-case time is O(S + R*C*3^L). Auxiliary space is O(S + L) for the trie and recursion, excluding the returned words.
